# Components and public contracts

Use the generated [API index](api/index.md); it contains 67 typed entrypoints for the 64 component entries plus the root, theme and foundation. Native barrel exports duplicate many secondary exports; prefer secondary imports for discovery and application code.

Read the specific contract before using a binding. Common differences from Neural Web:

| Concern | Native contract |
| --- | --- |
| Action | `NeuButtonComponent`, `neu-button`, required `label`, output `pressed` |
| Text control | `neu-input`, inherited `value`/`valueChange`, label, hint, required, disabled, readonly and validation inputs |
| Checkbox or Switch | `checked`/`checkedChange`, not a string `value` |
| Modal | Required `title`, `open`/`openChange`, `closed`, platform presentation events |
| Collections | `NeuOption` uses stable `id`, `label`, optional `description` and `disabled` |
| Data View | `items`, `query`, `descending`, `selected` and `refresh`; no Web Table row API |

The API references merge inherited input/output declarations; a binding absent from the derived class's own metadata may still be public. The references do not expose protected methods or Angular `ɵ` metadata. They do not authorize importing an internal physical file such as `@neural-ui/native/dist/foundation/mobile.js`.

Load collection states explicitly: loading, error, empty, populated, selected and disabled. Refresh emits an application request; provide real data loading or clearly explain an in-memory demonstration. Match the surrounding description to what the example actually does.

See [collections example](../examples/collections.ts), [forms](forms.md) and [customization](customization.md).

# Projection and typed templates

Choose the customization API actually exported by the component; Web's similarly named directives do not apply.

- Card and Panel accept projected content and their exported header/footer marker directives. Use native `view`/`text` inside them.
- Modal and Bottom Sheet project body content and export `NeuModalHeaderDirective`/`NeuModalFooterDirective` or their Bottom Sheet counterparts for `ng-template` slots. Keep title and close semantics accessible.
- Data View exports `NeuDataViewItemDirective` and `NeuDataViewItemContext`; Select exports item/selected directives and contexts. Listbox, Gallery and Virtual List have their own contracts. Read the corresponding [API entry](api/index.md) before choosing context fields.

For Select, the selected-template context contains the selected option array as `$implicit`, plus `value`, `values` and `placeholder`. Its item template uses the Listbox item context. Do not assume an undocumented `row`, `record`, `onSelect` or Web template variable.

The [overlay example](../examples/overlays.ts) uses a real `neuModalFooter` slot and application-owned `open` state. The supplied footer button closes the requested state; native presentation completion is a separate event. `dismissed` is an iOS native completion event and does not mean Android has failed when it is absent.

Avoid placing a second large modal/calendar over a constrained modal body unless the flow and the actual platform presentation support it. Verify overflow and dismissal on the target device, not only in the browser preview.

# Forms and owned state

Use writable signals in the application. An input's `value` model owns text; Checkbox/Switch use `checked`. Single Select uses string `value`; multiple Select uses `values: readonly string[]`. Keep option IDs stable when translating labels.

```html
<neu-input label="Full name" [(value)]="name" [required]="true" />
<neu-select label="Team" [options]="teams" [(value)]="team" />
<neu-checkbox label="Product updates" [(checked)]="updates" />
<neu-button label="Save profile" (pressed)="save()" />
```

Import every component used; see the complete [forms example](../examples/forms.ts). `pressed` requests an action, while the application validates and saves. Do not attach a Web `click` handler to a Native Neural component in place of its declared output.

Angular Signal Forms is optional. If used, import `FormField` from the matching `@angular/forms/signals` release and bind `[formField]` to the actual form tree field. Let that form own the control; do not also bind its `value`/`checked` model or a second form owner. Run strict Angular template checking for the actual field types. Classic CVA assumptions and Web Neural examples are not substitutes for checking the Native control.

Neural's `NeuFormFieldComponent` arranges projected content and messages. It is not Angular's `FormField` directive. Apply the accessible name and requirement to the projected control itself.

Localize exposed hint, error, empty, search and action labels. Check date/number contracts for supported formats instead of storing translated display strings as canonical values.

# Layout, accessibility and localization

Use native primitives and the app's safe-area shell. `SafeAreaProvider` supplies insets; `SafeAreaView` applies them. Respect all needed edges in landscape, not just the top inset in portrait. Let collection content scroll inside a bounded layout, and leave deliberate padding/gaps between labels, fields, cards and buttons.

`ScrollView`'s `contentContainerStyle` controls content padding/gap. When a focused field must not consume the first tap on another control, choose `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` for that flow and verify the actual renderer behavior. Avoid focusing a search input on opening every selection popup if that unnecessarily summons the mobile keyboard.

Give Neural buttons visible labels and icon actions useful accessible names through their declared inputs. Use native `text` for readable content. Keep selection visible without relying on color alone, and preserve reduced-motion behavior when styling transitions.

Translate the component's exposed action/search/empty/error/close labels and date locale. Keep option IDs and stored values independent of language. Preserve prerelease names such as Beta/Alpha as product/version terms rather than translating a package version.

Exercise each changed flow at a narrow width, both orientations, enlarged system text and light/dark themes. Check keyboard dismissal, scrolling, focus and return from overlays. Browser preview checks help catch clipping and action failures; they do not verify native VoiceOver/TalkBack announcements, touch exploration or native module availability. Report these as separate checks, with observed evidence rather than an accessibility certification.

# Navigation and composed screens

`NeuNavComponent` is a selection/navigation control, not an application router. Supply `NeuNavItem[]`, maintain the `value` model and handle `navigate` when the app needs a navigation side effect. Do not perform the same navigation in both valueChange and navigate.

The [navigation example](../examples/navigation.ts) changes real screen content through owned state. It is an in-memory example, not a claim that a native router or persisted history has been configured.

For an actual application stack, follow Angular Native's routing documentation and the generated app configuration. Neural emits actions and state; the app owns routes, back behavior and persistence. Do not transplant Web v2 routing providers, a browser URL strategy or a Web dock into a native app without checking the framework contract.

Keep a bottom navigation bar full-width in its intended layout, with readable labels and a clear selected state. Apply bottom safe-area insets at the app shell; do not add identical insets to both the shell and every nested screen. Provide distinct useful content for each destination.

# Native themes and tokens

Wrap a screen or app in `NeuThemeComponent` from `@neural-ui/native/theme`. `scheme` is `system`, `light` or `dark`. `tokens` is `Partial<NeuTokens>` from `@neural-ui/native/foundation`; `resolvedTokens` exposes the resolved read-only theme.

The generated [token contract](api/tokens.md) lists all 28 public `NeuTokens` properties. Numeric radius, spacing, fontSize and duration are native values, not CSS strings. Optional semantic text inks resolve from theme surfaces when omitted. Light and dark defaults are recorded in the generated API snapshot.

```ts
import type { NeuTokens } from '@neural-ui/native/foundation';
const brand = { accent: '#3b5bdb', onAccent: '#ffffff', radius: 16 } satisfies Partial<NeuTokens>;
```

Bind `[tokens]="brand"` to `neu-theme`. Fixed overrides apply in both modes, so use mode-specific values where a brand color needs different readable ink in dark mode. The [theme example](../examples/theme.ts) demonstrates a mode switch with a readable palette in each mode.

Use supported native styles and resolved `--neu-*` theme variables, such as `color: var(--neu-text)` or `background-color: var(--neu-surface)`. Do not copy the Web v2 catalogue's hundreds of CSS tokens or assume each is a Native override. Component-specific styles still belong to the actual renderer; browser DOM CSS and arbitrary layout features may not map to iOS/Android.

Preserve safe-area and text-scaling behavior when changing density. Customizing a theme does not justify changing a control's data or action contract.
